{{Short description|French mathematician}}
[[File:Michel Waldschmidt.jpg|thumb|Michel Waldschmidt in 2007 at [[Oberwolfach]]]]
'''Michel Waldschmidt''' (born June 17, 1946 at [[Nancy, France]]) is a French [[mathematician]], specializing in [[number theory]], especially [[transcendental number]]s.

== Career ==
Waldschmidt was educated at [[:fr:Lycée Henri Poincaré|Lycée Henri Poincaré]] and the [[University of Nancy]] until 1968. In 1972 he defended his thesis, titled ''Indépendance algébrique de nombres transcendants'' (Algebraic independence of transcendental numbers) and directed by Jean Fresnel, the [[University of Bordeaux]].

He was a research associate of the [[CNRS]] at the University of Bordeaux in 1971–1972. He was then a lecturer at [[Paris-Sud 11 University]] in 1972–1973. He became a lecturer at the [[University of Paris VI]] (Pierre et Marie Curie) and then became a professor there in 1973. He is a member of the {{Interlanguage link multi|Institut de mathématiques de Jussieu|fr|3=Institut de mathématiques de Jussieu|vertical-align=sup}}.

Waldschmidt was also a visiting professor at places including the [[École normale supérieure]]. 

From 2001 to 2004 he was president of the [[Mathematical Society of France]]. He is a member of several mathematical societies, including the [[European Mathematical Society|EMS]], the [[American Mathematical Society|AMS]] and [[Ramanujan Mathematical Society]].

==Awards and honors==
Waldschmidt was awarded the [[Albert Châtelet]] Prize in 1974, the [[CNRS Silver Medal]] in 1978, the Marquet Prize<ref>The "Prix Marquet" was established in 1605 by Barthélemy Marquet; see [https://books.google.com/books?id=f_dCtzspcusC&pg=PA385 Armorial du Dauphiné p.&nbsp;385].</ref> of [[Academy of Sciences (France)|Academy of Sciences]] in 1980 and the Special Award of the [[Godfrey Harold Hardy|Hardy]]–[[Ramanujan]] Society  in 1986. In 2021, he was awarded the Bertrand Russell Prize by the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite web |title=2021 Bertrand Russell Prize to Michel Waldschmidt |url=https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=6459 |website=American Mathematical Society |access-date=10 January 2021 |language=en}}</ref>
